title.raw: 卷九十七 志第四十五下: 食貨五 Volume 97 Treatises 50: Finance and Economics 5

sentences.zh: 食貨五

translations.literal: Finance and Economics 5
translations.idiomatic: Finance and Economics, Part Five

sentences.zh: 食貨前誌，據《經世大典》為之目，凡十有九，自天歷以前，載之詳矣。

translations.literal: The earlier monographs on finance and economics, taking their categories from the Jingshi Datian, number nineteen in all; for the period before the Tianli reign, the record is already detailed.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier treatises on finance and economics drew their chapter headings from the Jingshi Datian; there are nineteen sections in all, and for the period before the Tianli era the account is already thorough.

sentences.zh: 若夫元統以後，海運之多寡，鈔法之更變，鹽茶之利害，其見於《六條政類》之中，及有司采訪事跡，凡有足征者，具錄於篇，以備參考；

translations.literal: As for after the Yuantong era, the abundance or scarcity of maritime transport, changes in paper-currency law, and the benefits and harms of salt and tea—what appears in the Liutiao Zhenglei and in matters investigated by the responsible offices, wherever there is sufficient evidence, is fully recorded in these pages for reference;
translations.idiomatic: For the period after the Yuantong reign, whatever can be verified about fluctuations in sea transport, revisions to paper currency, and the gains and losses of the salt and tea monopolies—whether drawn from the Liutiao Zhenglei or from investigations by the relevant agencies—is recorded here in full for consultation.

sentences.zh: 而喪亂之際，其亡逸不存者，則闕之。

translations.literal: But in the time of ruin and disorder, what was lost and no longer survives has been left blank.
translations.idiomatic: Material lost in the chaos of collapse and no longer extant has been left blank.

sentences.zh: ○海運

translations.literal: ○ Maritime Transport
translations.idiomatic: Maritime Grain Transport

sentences.zh: 元自世祖用伯顏之言，歲漕東南粟，由海道以給京師，始自至元二十年，至於天歷、至順，由四萬石以上增而為三百萬以上，其所以為國計者大矣。

translations.literal: From the time when the Yuan, following Bayan's advice under Emperor Shizu, annually transported grain from the southeast by sea to supply the capital, beginning in the twentieth year of Zhiyuan and continuing through Tianli and Zhishun, the amount rose from more than forty thousand piculs to more than three million; its importance to state finance was great.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Shizu adopted Bayan's proposal to ship southeastern grain to the capital by sea each year, the annual volume grew from just over forty thousand piculs at the start in Zhiyuan 20 to more than three million by the Tianli and Zhishun reigns—a pillar of the dynasty's fiscal policy.

sentences.zh: 歷歲既久，弊日以生，水旱相仍，公私俱困，疲三省之民力，以充歲運之恒數，而押運監臨之官，與夫司出納之吏，恣為貪黷，腳價不以時給，收支不得其平，船戶貧乏，耗損益甚。

translations.literal: As the years passed, abuses arose daily; flood and drought followed one another, and public and private interests alike were strained. The labor of the three provinces was exhausted to meet the fixed annual quota, while the officials who escorted and supervised transport and the clerks who handled receipts and disbursements indulged in corruption at will; porterage fees were not paid on time, income and outgo fell out of balance, ship households grew destitute, and wastage increased ever more.
translations.idiomatic: Over time abuses multiplied: drought and flood came in succession, and both state and populace were squeezed dry. The three southeastern provinces were worked to exhaustion to meet the fixed annual quota, while escort officers, supervising officials, and treasury clerks plundered at will, porterage wages were paid late, accounts never balanced, ship owners fell into poverty, and losses mounted steadily.

sentences.zh: 兼以風濤不測，盜賊出沒，剽劫覆亡之患，自仍改至元之後，有不可勝言者矣。

translations.literal: Coupled with unpredictable winds and waves and the coming and going of bandits, the calamities of plunder and shipwreck after the change of reign title to Zhiyuan were beyond numbering.
translations.idiomatic: Unpredictable storms, roving pirates, and the disasters of raiding and sinking after the Zhiyuan reign change became too numerous to recount.

sentences.zh: 由是歲運之數，漸不如舊。

translations.literal: Because of this, the annual transport figures gradually fell short of former levels.
translations.idiomatic: For these reasons the annual haul gradually fell below earlier totals.

sentences.zh: 至正元年，益以河南之粟，通計江南三省所運，止得二百八十萬石。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhizheng, with Henan grain added in, the total transported from the three Jiangnan provinces amounted to only 2.8 million piculs.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 1, even counting Henan grain together with shipments from the three Jiangnan provinces, the total reached only 2.8 million piculs.

sentences.zh: 二年，又令江浙行省及中政院財賦總管府，撥賜諸人寺觀之糧，盡數起運，僅得二百六十萬石而已。

translations.literal: In the second year, the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat and the Central Secretariat's Bureau of Revenue were again ordered to mobilize for transport all grain allotted to temples and monasteries; only 2.6 million piculs were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the court also ordered the Jiang-Zhe Secretariat and the Central Secretariat revenue bureau to ship every picul of grain allocated to temples and monasteries, yet the total still reached only 2.6 million piculs.

sentences.zh: 及汝、潁倡亂，湖廣、江右相繼陷沒，而方國珍、張士誠竊據浙東、西之地，雖縻以好爵，資為藩屏，而貢賦不供，剝民以自奉，於是海運之舟不至京師者積年矣。

translations.literal: When rebellion broke out in Ru and Ying, Huguang and Jiangyou fell in succession, while Fang Guozhen and Zhang Shicheng seized eastern and western Zhejiang. Though they were bound with fine titles as a screen for the realm, they paid no tribute and stripped the people to support themselves; thus for years no maritime transport ships reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After revolt erupted in the Ru and Ying region and Huguang and Jiangyou fell one after another, Fang Guozhen and Zhang Shicheng carved up eastern and western Zhejiang. Though the court lavished noble ranks on them as supposed bulwarks of the realm, they withheld tribute and taxed the populace for their own upkeep, and for years no grain fleet reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 至十九年，朝廷遣兵部尚書伯顏帖木兒、戶部尚書齊履亨征海運於江浙，由海道至慶元，抵杭州。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, the court sent Minister of War Bayan Temür and Minister of Revenue Qi Lüheng to levy maritime transport in Jiang-Zhe; they went by sea to Qingyuan and reached Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year the court dispatched Minister of War Bayan Temür and Minister of Revenue Qi Lüheng to requisition sea transport in Jiang-Zhe; they sailed to Qingyuan and then proceeded to Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 時達識帖睦邇為江浙行中書省丞相，張士誠為太尉，方國珍為平章政事，詔命士誠輸粟，國珍具舟，達識帖睦邇總督之。

translations.literal: At that time Tash Temür was chief councillor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, Zhang Shicheng was Grand Marshal, and Fang Guozhen was Vice Councillor; the edict ordered Zhang to supply grain, Fang to provide ships, and Tash Temür to supervise overall.
translations.idiomatic: Tash Temür was then chief councillor of the Jiang-Zhe Secretariat, Zhang Shicheng held the title Grand Marshal, and Fang Guozhen was vice councillor. The edict assigned Zhang to furnish grain, Fang to supply vessels, and Tash Temür to supervise the operation.

sentences.zh: 既達朝廷之命，而方、張互相猜疑，士誠慮方氏載其粟而不以輸於京也，國珍恐張氏掣其舟而因乘虛以襲己也。

translations.literal: Once the court's orders had arrived, Fang and Zhang suspected each other: Zhang feared the Fang clan would load his grain but not deliver it to the capital, while Fang feared the Zhang clan would hold back his ships and seize the chance to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: After the imperial orders arrived, the two warlords distrusted each other. Zhang worried that Fang would load his grain but never send it to the capital; Fang feared Zhang would detain his fleet and strike while he was exposed.

sentences.zh: 伯顏帖木兒白於丞相，正辭以責之，巽言以諭之，乃釋二家之疑，克濟其事。

translations.literal: Bayan Temür reported to the chief councillor, rebuked them in direct terms, and admonished them in mild words, thereby dispelling the suspicions of both houses and bringing the matter to completion.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan Temür reported to the chief councillor, rebuked both sides in plain terms and reasoned with them gently, dispelled their mutual suspicions, and brought the transport through.

sentences.zh: 先率海舟俟於嘉興之澉浦，而平江之粟展轉以達杭之石墩，又一舍而後抵澉浦，乃載於舟。

translations.literal: He first led the sea vessels to wait at Ganpu in Jiaxing, while the grain of Pingjiang was relayed stage by stage to Shidun in Hangzhou; after one more stage it reached Ganpu and was loaded aboard.
translations.idiomatic: Sea vessels were first stationed at Ganpu in Jiaxing while Pingjiang grain was relayed in stages to Shidun near Hangzhou, then carried one more leg to Ganpu before loading.

sentences.zh: 海灘淺澀，躬履艱苦，粟之載於舟者，為石十有一萬。

translations.literal: The seashore was shallow and difficult; he personally endured hardship, and the grain loaded on the ships amounted to 110,000 piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The coast was shallow and treacherous; he endured the hardship in person, and the ships finally carried 110,000 piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 二十年五月赴京。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twentieth year they proceeded to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the twentieth year the fleet reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，又遣戶部尚書王宗禮等至江浙。

translations.literal: That autumn, the Minister of Revenue Wang Zongli and others were again sent to Jiang-Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the court again sent Minister of Revenue Wang Zongli and others to Jiang-Zhe.

sentences.zh: 二十一年五月，運糧赴京，如上年之數。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twenty-first year grain was transported to the capital in the same amount as the previous year.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the twenty-first year grain reached the capital in the same quantity as before.

sentences.zh: 九月，又遣兵部尚書徹徹不花、侍郎韓祺往征海運一百萬石。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Minister of War Cheche Buhua and Vice Minister Han Qi were again sent to levy one million piculs of maritime transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the court again dispatched Minister of War Cheche Buhua and Vice Minister Han Qi to requisition one million piculs by sea.

sentences.zh: 二十二年五月，運糧赴京，視上年之數，僅加二萬而已。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twenty-second year grain was sent to the capital; compared with the previous year's figure, it increased by only twenty thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the twenty-second year the fleet reached the capital with only twenty thousand piculs more than the year before.

sentences.zh: 九月，遣戶部尚書脫脫歡察爾、兵部尚書帖木至江浙。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Minister of Revenue Toghto Qanchar and Minister of War Temür were sent to Jiang-Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Minister of Revenue Toghto Qanchar and Minister of War Temür were sent to Jiang-Zhe.

sentences.zh: 二十三年五月，仍運糧十有三萬石赴京。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twenty-third year, 130,000 piculs of grain were again transported to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the twenty-third year 130,000 piculs were again shipped to the capital.

sentences.zh: 九月，又遣戶部侍郎博羅帖木兒、監丞賽因不花往征海運。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Vice Minister of Revenue Boluo Temür and Supervisor Sayin Buqa were again sent to levy maritime transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Vice Minister Boluo Temür and Supervisor Sayin Buqa were again dispatched to collect sea transport.

sentences.zh: 士誠托辭以拒命，由是東南之粟給京師者，遂止於是歲云。

translations.literal: Zhang Shicheng pleaded excuses to refuse the order; thus grain from the southeast supplying the capital ceased from that year onward.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng pleaded pretexts and refused; from that year onward southeastern grain no longer reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 至正十年，右丞相脫脫欲更鈔法，乃會中書省、樞密院、御史臺及集賢、翰林兩院官共議之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhizheng, the Right Chancellor Toghto wished to change the paper-currency system and convened officials of the Secretariat, Privy Council, Censorate, and the Academies of Scholarly Worthies and Hanlin to discuss it jointly.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 10 Right Chancellor Toghto proposed revising paper currency and convened officials from the Secretariat, Privy Council, Censorate, and the Academies of Scholarly Worthies and Hanlin to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 先是，左司都事武祺嘗建言云：「鈔法自世祖時已行之後，除撥支料本、倒易昏鈔以布天下外，有合支名目，於寶鈔總庫料鈔轉撥，所以鈔法疏通，民受其利。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wu Qi, director of the Left Secretariat, had submitted a proposal saying: 'After the paper-currency system had been in force since Emperor Shizu's time, apart from allocating reserve funds and exchanging worn notes to circulate them throughout the realm, all items payable under statute were to be transferred through reserve notes at the general treasury of precious notes, whereby the currency system remained unblocked and the people benefited.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wu Qi, a director in the Left Secretariat, had argued: 'Since Emperor Shizu established paper currency, aside from setting aside reserve funds and exchanging worn notes nationwide, every statutory payment was supposed to pass through reserve notes at the general treasury—keeping circulation smooth and benefiting the people.

sentences.zh: 比年以來，失祖宗元行鈔法本意。

translations.literal: In recent years the original intent of the ancestral paper-currency system has been lost.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the court has abandoned the original intent of the ancestral currency policy.

sentences.zh: 不與轉撥，故民間流轉者少，致偽鈔滋多。」

translations.literal: Because transfer payments were not made, few notes circulated among the people, and counterfeit notes multiplied.'
translations.idiomatic: Without those transfers, notes scarcely circulated among the populace, and counterfeits proliferated.'

sentences.zh: 遂準其所言，凡合支名目，已於總庫轉支。

translations.literal: His proposal was approved, and all statutory payments were transferred through the general treasury.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his proposal, and all statutory payments were again routed through the general treasury.

sentences.zh: 至是，吏部尚書偰哲篤及武祺，俱欲迎合丞相之意。

translations.literal: At this juncture, Minister of Personnel Jiezhidu and Wu Qi both wished to curry favor with the chancellor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: By then Minister of Personnel Jiezhidu and Wu Qi were both eager to align themselves with the chancellor.

sentences.zh: 偰哲篤言更鈔法，以楮幣一貫文省權銅錢一千文為母，而錢為子。

translations.literal: Jiezhidu spoke of changing the currency law, making one string of paper notes (worth one thousand cash in standard weight) the parent and cash the child.
translations.idiomatic: Jiezhidu urged a new currency scheme in which one standard string of paper notes, equivalent to one thousand cash, would be the parent and coin the child.

sentences.zh: 眾人皆唯唯，不敢出一語，惟集賢大學士兼國子祭酒呂思誠獨奮然曰：「中統、至元自有母子，上料為母，下料為子。

translations.literal: Everyone murmured assent and dared not utter a word, but only Grand Academician of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies and Rector of the Imperial College Lü Sicheng spoke up boldly: 'Zhongtong and Zhiyuan notes already have their parent and child—the higher denomination is parent, the lower is child.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone murmured agreement and stayed silent, until Grand Academician and Imperial College Rector Lü Sicheng alone spoke up boldly: 'The Zhongtong and Zhiyuan notes already have parent and child—the higher denomination is parent, the lower is child.

sentences.zh: 比之達達人乞養漢人為子，是終為漢人之子而已，豈有故紙為父，而以銅為過房兒子者乎！」

translations.literal: It is like a Mongol asking to adopt a Han as son—he ends up merely a Han's son; how could old paper be father and copper an adopted son!'
translations.idiomatic: It is like a Mongol asking to adopt a Han as his son—he still ends up a Han's son in the end. How can worn paper be the father and copper an adopted heir!'

sentences.zh: 一坐皆笑。

translations.literal: The whole assembly laughed.
translations.idiomatic: The whole room burst out laughing.

sentences.zh: 思誠又曰：「錢鈔用法，以虛換實，其致一也。

translations.literal: Sicheng added: 'In the use of cash and notes, the insubstantial is exchanged for the substantial—the principle is the same.
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng went on: 'Whether using coin or notes, the insubstantial stands in for the substantial—the principle is the same.

sentences.zh: 今歷代錢及至正錢，中統鈔及至元鈔、交鈔，分為五項，若下民知之，藏其實而棄其虛，恐非國之利也。」

translations.literal: Now dynastic cash and Zhizheng cash, Zhongtong notes, Zhiyuan notes, and Jiaochao are divided into five categories; if the common people understand this, they will hoard the substantial and discard the insubstantial—surely that is not to the state's advantage.'
translations.idiomatic: If you split circulation into five categories—old and new coin, Zhongtong notes, Zhiyuan notes, and Jiaochao—the people will hoard what is real and discard what is paper. That can hardly benefit the state.'

sentences.zh: 偰哲篤、武祺又曰：「至元鈔多偽，故更之爾。」

translations.literal: Jiezhidu and Wu Qi said again: 'Zhiyuan notes are largely counterfeit, hence the change.'
translations.idiomatic: Jiezhidu and Wu Qi replied: 'Zhiyuan notes are widely counterfeited—that is why we must change them.'

sentences.zh: 思誠曰：「至元鈔非偽，人為偽爾，交鈔若出，亦有偽者矣。

translations.literal: Sicheng said: 'Zhiyuan notes are not counterfeit—men make them counterfeit; if Jiaochao is issued, there will be counterfeits as well.
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng retorted: 'The Zhiyuan notes are not false—the forgers are. Issue Jiaochao and you will have forgeries of that too.

sentences.zh: 且至元鈔猶故戚也，家之童稚皆識之矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, Zhiyuan notes are like old kin—every child in the household knows them.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Zhiyuan notes are like old relatives—even children in every household know them.

sentences.zh: 交鈔猶新戚也，雖不敢不親，人未識也，其偽反滋多爾。

translations.literal: Jiaochao is like new kin—though one dare not fail to treat them with respect, people do not yet know them, and counterfeits will only increase all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaochao would be like new kin—people must accept it, yet they do not know it, and counterfeits would multiply all the more.

sentences.zh: 況祖宗成憲，豈可輕改。」

translations.literal: Moreover, the settled statutes of the ancestors—how can they be lightly altered?'
translations.idiomatic: And how can you lightly alter the settled institutions of the ancestors?'

sentences.zh: 偰哲篤曰：「祖宗法弊，亦可改矣。」

translations.literal: Jiezhidu said: 'When ancestral laws are defective, they too may be changed.'
translations.idiomatic: Jiezhidu said: 'When ancestral institutions fail, they too may be changed.'

sentences.zh: 思誠曰：「汝輩更法，又欲上誣世皇，是汝又欲與世皇爭高下也。

translations.literal: Sicheng said: 'You people change the law and also wish to cast blame upward on Emperor Shizu—you wish to vie with Emperor Shizu for superiority.
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng said: 'By changing the law you would slander Emperor Shizu from above—you are trying to outdo the founding emperor himself.

sentences.zh: 且自世皇以來，諸帝皆謚曰孝，改其成憲，可謂孝乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover, since Emperor Shizu's time every emperor has been given the posthumous title Xiao ('Filial'); to alter his settled statutes—can that be called filial?'
translations.idiomatic: Every emperor since Shizu has borne the posthumous title 'Filial.' Is it filial to overturn his settled institutions?'

sentences.zh: 武祺又欲錢鈔兼行，思誠曰：「錢鈔兼行，輕重不倫，何者為母，何者為子？

translations.literal: Wu Qi again wished cash and notes to circulate together. Sicheng said: 'If cash and notes circulate together, light and heavy are not in proper relation—which is parent, which is child?
translations.idiomatic: Wu Qi again urged concurrent circulation of coin and notes. Sicheng said: 'If coin and notes circulate together, their relative weight is out of order—which is parent and which is child?

sentences.zh: 汝不通古今，道聽途說，何足以行，徒以口舌取媚大臣，可乎？」

translations.literal: You do not understand past and present, you repeat hearsay—how is that sufficient to put into practice? You merely use your tongue to flatter great ministers—is that acceptable?'
translations.idiomatic: You know neither past nor present and repeat street gossip—how can that be policy? You only flatter powerful ministers with your tongue—is that acceptable?'

sentences.zh: 偰哲篤曰：「我等策既不可行，公有何策？」

translations.literal: Jiezhidu said: 'Since our plan cannot be carried out, what plan do you have?'
translations.idiomatic: Jiezhidu asked: 'If our plan will not work, what is yours?'

sentences.zh: 思誠曰：「我有三字策，曰行不得，行不得。」

translations.literal: Sicheng said: 'I have a three-character plan: it cannot be done, it cannot be done.'
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng answered: 'I have a three-word plan: it cannot be done, it cannot be done.'

sentences.zh: 又曰：「丞相勿聽此言。

translations.literal: He added: 'Chancellor, do not heed these words.
translations.idiomatic: He added: 'Chancellor, do not listen to them.

sentences.zh: 如向日開金口河，成則歸功汝等，不成則歸罪丞相矣。」

translations.literal: As when the Jinkou River was opened the other day—if it succeeds, the credit goes to you; if it fails, the blame falls on the chancellor.'
translations.idiomatic: Remember the Jinkou River project: if it succeeds they take the credit; if it fails the chancellor bears the blame."

sentences.zh: 脫脫見其言直，猶豫未決。

translations.literal: Toghto, seeing his words were blunt, hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Toghto, struck by his blunt honesty, hesitated and could not decide.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫也先帖木兒言曰：「呂祭酒言有是者，有非者，但不當坐廟堂高聲厲色。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Yeshi Temür said: 'Rector Lü's words have points that are right and points that are wrong, but he ought not to sit in the hall of state shouting in a harsh voice.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Yeshi Temür said: 'Rector Lü is partly right and partly wrong, but he should not shout in the council chamber.

sentences.zh: 若從其言，此事終不行耶！」

translations.literal: If we follow his words, will this matter never be carried out!'
translations.idiomatic: If we heed him, will the reform never go forward!'

sentences.zh: 明日，諷御史劾之，思誠歸臥不出，遂定更鈔之議而奏之。

translations.literal: The next day he prompted the censors to impeach him; Sicheng returned home, lay in bed, and did not go out; the decision to change the notes was then settled and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he prompted the censors to impeach Lü, who stayed home in bed. The currency reform was then settled and memorialized.

sentences.zh: 下詔云：「朕聞帝王之治，因時制宜，損益之方，在乎通變。

translations.literal: An edict was issued saying: 'We have heard that in the governance of emperors and kings, measures are fitted to the times; the method of increase and decrease lies in flexible adaptation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: 'We have heard that sage rulers adapt policy to the times; the art of reform lies in timely change.

sentences.zh: 惟我世祖皇帝，建元之初，頒行中統交鈔，以錢為文，雖鼓鑄之規未遑，而錢幣兼行之意已具。

translations.literal: Our Emperor Shizu, at the beginning of his reign, promulgated Zhongtong Jiaochao with cash as the denomination; though the regulations for minting had not yet been completed, the intent of circulating cash and notes together was already in place.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of his reign Emperor Shizu issued Zhongtong Jiaochao denominated in cash; though minting rules were not yet complete, the intent to circulate coin and notes together was already established.

sentences.zh: 厥後印造至元寶鈔，以一當五，名曰子母相權，而錢實未用。

translations.literal: Thereafter Zhiyuan precious notes were printed, one note equaling five, called 'parent and child balancing each other,' but cash was in fact not used.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhiyuan notes were issued at a one-to-five ratio, called 'parent and child in mutual balance,' though coin was never actually put into circulation.

sentences.zh: 歷歲滋久，鈔法偏虛，物價騰踴，奸偽日萌，民用匱乏。

translations.literal: As the years lengthened, the note system grew ever more insubstantial, prices soared, fraud daily sprouted, and the people's use grew impoverished.
translations.idiomatic: Over the years the currency grew hollow, prices soared, counterfeiting spread, and the populace was left destitute.

sentences.zh: 爰詢廷臣，博采輿論，僉謂拯弊必合更張。

translations.literal: We therefore questioned court ministers and broadly gathered public opinion; all agreed that to save the abuses a thorough change was necessary.
translations.idiomatic: We consulted court ministers and gathered public opinion; all agreed that rescuing the system required thorough reform.

sentences.zh: 其以中統交鈔壹貫文省權銅錢一千文，準至元寶鈔二貫，仍鑄至正通寶錢與歷代銅錢並用，以實鈔法。

translations.literal: Let one string of Zhongtong Jiaochao (standard weight) be equivalent to one thousand cash in copper, equal to two strings of Zhiyuan precious notes; let Zhizheng Tongbao cash still be minted and used together with cash of successive dynasties to substantiate the note system.
translations.idiomatic: One standard string of Zhongtong Jiaochao shall equal one thousand cash and two strings of Zhiyuan notes; Zhizheng Tongbao shall be minted and circulate alongside earlier coin to back the paper currency.

sentences.zh: 至元寶鈔，通行如故。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan precious notes shall continue to circulate as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan notes shall continue to circulate as before.

sentences.zh: 子母相權，新舊相濟，上副世祖立法之初意。」

translations.literal: Parent and child balancing each other, new and old supporting each other—this accords with the original intent of Emperor Shizu's legislation.'
translations.idiomatic: Parent and child in balance, new and old in support—fulfilling the founding intent of Emperor Shizu's monetary law.'

sentences.zh: 十一年，置寶泉提舉司，掌鼓鑄至正通寶錢、印造交鈔，令民間通用。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Baocuan Intendant Office was established to oversee minting of Zhizheng Tongbao cash and printing of Jiaochao, ordering general use among the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the Baocuan Intendant Office was established to mint Zhizheng Tongbao and print Jiaochao for general circulation.

sentences.zh: 行之未久，物價騰踴，價逾十倍。

translations.literal: Not long after it was put into practice, prices soared to more than ten times their former level.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after implementation prices more than tripled—indeed rose tenfold.

sentences.zh: 又值海內大亂，軍儲供給，賞賜犒勞，每日印造，不可數計。

translations.literal: Moreover, great disorder arose throughout the realm; for military stores, supplies, rewards, and consolation payments, notes were printed daily beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile civil war engulfed the realm; military supplies, rewards, and consolation payments required daily printing beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 舟車裝運，軸轤相接，交料之散滿人間者，無處無之。

translations.literal: Ships and carts loaded them in transport, axle to axle; reserve notes scattered among the people were everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Ships and carts hauled endless loads, axle to axle; paper money lay scattered everywhere.

sentences.zh: 昏軟者不復行用。

translations.literal: Worn and soft notes were no longer accepted in circulation.
translations.idiomatic: Worn, limp notes were no longer accepted.

sentences.zh: 京師料鈔十錠，易鬥粟不可得。

translations.literal: In the capital, ten ingots of reserve notes could not buy a dou of grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital ten ingots of reserve notes could not buy a single dou of grain.

sentences.zh: 既而所在郡縣，皆以物貨相貿易，公私所積之鈔，遂俱不行，人視之若弊楮，而國用由是遂乏矣。

translations.literal: Before long every prefecture and county traded in goods instead; notes accumulated by public and private parties alike ceased to circulate; people regarded them as worthless paper, and state revenue thereby grew deficient.
translations.idiomatic: Soon every prefecture and county bartered in kind; public and private hoards of notes alike ceased to circulate; people treated them as scrap paper, and state finances collapsed.

sentences.zh: 大都之鹽：元統二年四月，御史臺備監察御史言：「竊睹京畿居民繁盛，日用之中，鹽不可闕。

translations.literal: Salt in Dadu: In the fourth month of the second year of Yuantong, the Censorate reported a supervising censor's memorial saying: 'We observe that the capital region's population is dense; in daily life salt cannot be lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Salt in Dadu: In the fourth month of Yuantong 2 the Censorate relayed a supervising censor's memorial: 'The capital region is densely populated, and salt is indispensable in daily life.

sentences.zh: 大德中，因商販把握行市，民食貴鹽，乃置局設官賣之。

translations.literal: In the Dade era, because merchants controlled the market, the people ate costly salt, and bureaus were therefore established with officials to sell it.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dade era merchants cornered the market and salt grew costly, so the government set up bureaus to sell it directly.

sentences.zh: 中統鈔一貫，買鹽四斤八兩。

translations.literal: One string of Zhongtong notes bought four jin and eight liang of salt.
translations.idiomatic: One string of Zhongtong notes bought four jin eight liang of salt.

sentences.zh: 後雖倍其價，猶敷民用。

translations.literal: Later, though the price was doubled, it still sufficed for the people's use.
translations.idiomatic: Even after the price was doubled, households could still afford it.

sentences.zh: 及泰定間，因所任局官不得其人，在上者失於鈐束，致有短少之弊。

translations.literal: By the Taiding era, because unsuitable men were appointed bureau officials and superiors failed in restraint, the abuse of short-weight arose.
translations.idiomatic: By the Taiding era unsuitable bureau officers were appointed, superiors failed to enforce discipline, and short-weighting became common.

sentences.zh: 於是巨商趨利者營屬當道，以局官侵盜為由，輒奏罷之，復從民販賣。

translations.literal: Thereupon great merchants seeking profit cultivated connections with those in power, cited bureau officials' embezzlement as the reason, and promptly memorialized to abolish the bureaus, restoring private merchant sales.
translations.idiomatic: Great merchants then cultivated patrons at court, cited bureau corruption, and had the offices abolished so private trade could resume.

sentences.zh: 自是鈔一貫，僅買鹽一斤。

translations.literal: From then on one string of notes bought only one jin of salt.
translations.idiomatic: From then on one string bought only one jin of salt.

sentences.zh: 無籍之徒，私相犯界，煎賣獨受其利，官課為所侵礙。

translations.literal: Ruffians without registration privately crossed boundaries to boil and sell salt, keeping the profit to themselves and encroaching on official revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Unlicensed ruffians illegally crossed salting boundaries, boiled and sold salt for private profit, and encroached on official revenue.

sentences.zh: 而民食貴鹽益甚，貧者多不得食，甚不副朝廷恤小民之意。

translations.literal: Yet the people ate ever costlier salt; many of the poor could not obtain it—greatly failing to accord with the court's intent to care for the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Salt grew ever costlier; many poor households could no longer afford it—far from the court's intent to care for common people.

sentences.zh: 如朝廷仍舊設局，官為發賣，庶課不虧，而民受賜矣。」

translations.literal: If the court re-establishes the bureaus and officials sell on its behalf, perhaps revenue will not suffer loss and the people will receive benefit.'
translations.idiomatic: If the court restores the bureaus and sells salt directly, revenue need not suffer and the people will benefit.'

sentences.zh: 既而大都路備三巡院及大興、宛平縣所申，又戶部尚書建言，皆如御史所陳。

translations.literal: Thereafter the Dadu Circuit reported the petitions of the three patrol offices and of Daxing and Wanping counties, and the Minister of Revenue also submitted a proposal—all matching what the censor had stated.
translations.idiomatic: The Dadu Circuit then relayed petitions from the three patrol offices and from Daxing and Wanping counties, and the Minister of Revenue memorialized in the same terms as the censor.

sentences.zh: 戶部乃言，以謂「榷鹽之法，本以裕國而便民。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue then stated, saying: 'The salt monopoly law was originally meant to enrich the state and benefit the people.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue replied: 'The salt monopoly was originally meant to enrich the state and benefit the people.

sentences.zh: 始自大德七年罷大都運司，令河間運司兼辦。

translations.literal: Beginning in the seventh year of Dade the Dadu Transport Commission was abolished and the Hejian Transport Commission was ordered to handle it concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 7 the Dadu Transport Commission was abolished and the Hejian commission took over.

sentences.zh: 每歲存留鹽數，散之米鋪，從其發賣。

translations.literal: Each year the retained salt quota was distributed to rice shops for them to sell.
translations.idiomatic: Each year's retained salt quota was distributed to rice shops for resale.

sentences.zh: 後因富商專利，遂於南北二城設局，凡十有五處，官為賣之。

translations.literal: Later, because wealthy merchants monopolized profits, bureaus were set up in the northern and southern cities—fifteen in all—with officials selling on the government's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because wealthy merchants monopolized profits, fifteen bureaus were set up in the northern and southern cities for official sale.

sentences.zh: 當時立法嚴明，民甚便益。

translations.literal: At that time the legislation was strict and clear, and the people were greatly benefited.
translations.idiomatic: The regulations were then strict and clear, and the people benefited greatly.

sentences.zh: 泰定二年，因局官綱船人等多有侵盜之弊，復從民販賣，而罷所置之局。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiding, because bureau officials, transport-boat men, and others had many abuses of embezzlement, private merchant sales were restored and the established bureaus were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiding 2, citing corruption among bureau staff and transport crews, the government restored private sales and abolished the bureaus.

sentences.zh: 未及數載，有司屢言富商高擡價直之害。

translations.literal: Before several years had passed, responsible offices repeatedly reported the harm of wealthy merchants raising prices.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years officials repeatedly reported the harm of merchants raising prices.

sentences.zh: 運司所言綱船作弊，蓋因立法不嚴，失於關防所致。

translations.literal: The transport commission's claim of cheating by transport-boat men was fundamentally because legislation was not strict and control and inspection failed.
translations.idiomatic: Transport-boat fraud, as the commission alleged, stemmed from lax legislation and failed oversight.

sentences.zh: 且各處俱有官設鹽鋪，與商賈販賣並無窒礙，豈有京城之內，乃革罷官賣之局。

translations.literal: Moreover, everywhere there are government salt shops, which do not obstruct merchant sales—how could it be that within the capital alone the bureaus for official sale were abolished?
translations.idiomatic: Every region has government salt shops alongside merchant trade without conflict—why abolish official sale only in the capital?

sentences.zh: 宜準本部尚書所言，及大都路所申，依舊制於南北二城置局十有五處。

translations.literal: It is appropriate to approve what this ministry's minister stated and what the Dadu Circuit reported, and according to the former system establish fifteen bureaus in the northern and southern cities.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry recommends approving the minister's proposal and the Dadu Circuit's petition, and restoring fifteen bureaus in the northern and southern cities under the former system.

sentences.zh: 每局日賣十引，設賣鹽官二員，以歲一周為滿，責其奉公發賣。

translations.literal: Each bureau shall sell ten yin daily; two salt-selling officials shall be appointed, with one year as the term of office, charged to sell dutifully in the public interest.
translations.idiomatic: Each bureau shall sell ten yin per day, with two salt officers appointed for one-year terms and charged to sell faithfully in the public interest.

sentences.zh: 每中統鈔一貫，買鹽二斤四兩，毋令雜灰土其中，及權衡不得其平。

translations.literal: For each string of Zhongtong notes, two jin four liang of salt may be bought; they must not mix ash or earth into it, nor allow the balance to be uneven.
translations.idiomatic: One string of Zhongtong notes shall buy two jin four liang of salt, without adulteration or false weights.

sentences.zh: 凡買鹽過十貫者禁之，不及貫者從所買與之。

translations.literal: Purchases of salt exceeding ten strings are forbidden; for amounts under one string, sell according to what is bought.
translations.idiomatic: Purchases exceeding ten strings are forbidden; for amounts under one string, sell the amount requested.

sentences.zh: 如滿歲無短少失陷及元定分數者，減一界升用之；

translations.literal: If at year's end there is no shortfall, loss, or failure to meet the original fixed quota, reduce one term of service and promote them;
translations.idiomatic: If at year's end there is no shortfall, loss, or failure to meet the fixed quota, reduce one term of service and promote them;

sentences.zh: 若有侵盜者，依例追斷其合賣鹽數。

translations.literal: if there is embezzlement, pursue and punish according to statute the amount of salt they should have sold.
translations.idiomatic: if there is embezzlement, pursue and punish according to statute for the salt they should have sold.

sentences.zh: 令河間運司分為四季，起赴京廒，用官定法物，兩平稱收，分給各局。

translations.literal: Order the Hejian Transport Commission to divide deliveries into four seasons, transport them to the capital granaries, receive them on the even balance with official standard weights, and distribute to each bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The Hejian Transport Commission shall deliver in four seasonal shipments to the capital depots, receive them on official standard scales, and distribute to each bureau.

sentences.zh: 其所賣價鈔，逐旬起解，委本部官輪次提調之。

translations.literal: The note proceeds from sales shall be forwarded every ten days, with officials of this ministry assigned in rotation to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: Sale proceeds in notes shall be remitted every ten days under rotating supervision by ministry officials.

sentences.zh: 仍委官巡視，如有豪強兼利之徒，頻買局鹽而增價轉賣於外者，從提調巡督官痛治之。

translations.literal: Officials are still to be commissioned to inspect; if there are powerful men seeking double profit who frequently buy bureau salt and resell it outside at raised prices, the supervising and patrol officials in charge of oversight shall severely punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Inspectors shall remain posted; any powerful profiteer who repeatedly buys bureau salt and resells it outside at inflated prices shall be severely punished by the supervising officials.

sentences.zh: 仍令運司嚴督押運之人，設法防禁，毋致縱令綱船人等作弊。

translations.literal: Still order the transport commission strictly to supervise escort personnel, devise methods of prevention, and not allow transport-boat men and others to cheat.
translations.idiomatic: The transport commission shall strictly supervise escort crews and prevent transport-boat crews from cheating.

sentences.zh: 其客商鹽貨，從便相參發賣。」

translations.literal: Merchant salt goods may be sold concurrently as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Merchant salt may be sold alongside as convenient."

sentences.zh: 四月二十六日，中書省上奏，如戶部所擬行之。

translations.literal: On the twenty-sixth day of the fourth month, the Secretariat memorialized and implemented it as the Ministry of Revenue proposed.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-sixth day of the fourth month the Secretariat memorialized and approved the Ministry of Revenue proposal.

sentences.zh: 至元三年三月，大都京廒申戶部云：「近奉文帖，起運至元二年京廒發賣食鹽一萬五千引，令兩平稱收，如數具實申部。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year of Zhiyuan, the Dadu capital granaries reported to the Ministry of Revenue: "Recently, following documents, we transported 15,000 yin of salt for sale from the Zhiyuan 2 capital granaries, ordered receipt on the even balance, and truthfully reported the full amount to the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Zhiyuan 3 the Dadu capital granaries reported to the Ministry of Revenue: "Pursuant to recent orders we transported 15,000 yin of salt from the Zhiyuan 2 capital stock for sale, received on the even balance, and reported the full amount to the ministry.

sentences.zh: 除各綱淹沒短少鹽計八百四十八引，本廒實收一萬四千一百五十有二引，已支一萬一百引付各局發賣，見存鹽四千五十有二引，支撥欲盡。

translations.literal: Apart from 848 yin lost or short through sinking of transport convoys, the granaries actually received 14,152 yin; 10,100 yin have been disbursed to the bureaus for sale; 4,052 yin remain on hand and disbursement is nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: After deducting 848 yin lost or short from sunk convoys, the granaries actually received 14,152 yin; 10,100 yin were issued to the bureaus for sale; only 4,052 yin remain and stock is nearly exhausted.

sentences.zh: 所據至元三年食鹽，宜依例於河間運司起運一萬五千引赴都，庶民間食用不闕。」

translations.literal: The salt for Zhiyuan 3 should, according to precedent, be transported 15,000 yin from the Hejian Transport Commission to the capital, so that the people's daily consumption is not lacking.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan 3 salt should, as usual, be transported 15,000 yin from the Hejian commission to the capital so households do not go without.'

sentences.zh: 戶部準其所言，乃議：「京廒食鹽，今歲宜從河間運一萬五千引，其腳價席索等費，令運司於鹽課錢內通算支用。

translations.literal: The ministry approved their statement and deliberated: 'Capital granary salt this year should be transported 15,000 yin from Hejian; porterage, matting, rope, and other costs shall be paid in lump sum from salt-tax revenue by the transport commission.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry approved and proposed: 'This year the capital should receive 15,000 yin from Hejian; porterage, matting, and rope costs shall be drawn from salt-tax revenue by the transport commission.

sentences.zh: 仍召募有產業船戶，互相保識，每一千引為一綱，就差各該場官一員，並本司奏差或監運巡鹽官，每名管押一綱，於大都興國等場見收鹽內驗數，分派分司官監視，如數兩平支收，限三月內赴京廒交卸，取文憑赴部銷照。

translations.literal: Still recruit ship households with property who mutually guarantee one another; each 1,000 yin form one convoy; appoint one salt-field official from each relevant field, together with the commission's memorial envoy or transport-supervising salt-patrol official—each supervising one convoy; verify quantities from salt received at Xingguo and other Dadu fields; assign branch officials to oversee; receive on the even balance in full; deliver to capital granaries within three months, obtain documents, and present them to the ministry for cancellation.
translations.idiomatic: Recruit property-owning ship households under mutual guarantee; form convoys of 1,000 yin each; assign one field official plus a commission envoy or salt patrol officer per convoy; verify quantities at Xingguo and other Dadu depots under branch supervision; receive on the even balance; deliver to capital granaries within three months and obtain cancellation documents from the ministry.

sentences.zh: 但有雜和沙土，濕潤短少數，並令本綱船戶、押運場官、奏差監運諸人，如數均賠，依例坐罪。」

translations.literal: If there is mixing with sand or earth, dampness, or short quantity, order the convoy ship households, escort field officials, memorial envoys, transport supervisors, and all others to compensate equally in full and be punished according to statute.'
translations.idiomatic: Any adulteration with sand or earth, dampness, or short weight shall be compensated equally by convoy crews, escort officials, envoys, and supervisors, who shall be punished according to statute.'

sentences.zh: 中書如戶部所議行之。

translations.literal: The Secretariat implemented it as the Ministry of Revenue deliberated.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat approved the Ministry of Revenue plan.

sentences.zh: 至正三年，監察御史王思誠、侯思禮等建言：「京師自大德七年罷大都鹽運司，設官賣鹽，置局十有五處，泰定二年以其不便罷之，元統二年又復之，迨今十年，法久弊生。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhizheng, supervising censors Wang Sicheng, Hou Sili, and others submitted a proposal: 'Since the seventh year of Dade, when the Dadu Salt Transport Commission was abolished in the capital, official salt sales were established and fifteen bureaus set up; in the second year of Taiding they were abolished as inconvenient; in the second year of Yuantong they were restored; until now ten years have passed and long-standing law has bred abuses.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 3 supervising censors Wang Sicheng, Hou Sili, and others proposed: 'Since Dade 7 the Dadu Salt Transport Commission was abolished and fifteen official salt bureaus were set up; Taiding 2 abolished them as inconvenient; Yuantong 2 restored them; ten years on, entrenched abuses have appeared.

sentences.zh: 在船則有侵盜滲溺之患，入局則有和雜灰土之奸。

translations.literal: On ship there are the troubles of embezzlement and seepage; in the bureau there is the fraud of mixing ash and earth.
translations.idiomatic: At sea there is embezzlement and leakage; in the bureaus there is adulteration with ash and earth.

sentences.zh: 名曰一貫二斤四兩，實不得一斤之上。

translations.literal: It is called one string for two jin four liang, but in fact one does not receive even one jin.
translations.idiomatic: The price is one string for two jin four liang, but buyers receive less than one jin.

sentences.zh: 其潔凈不雜，而斤兩足者，唯上司提調數處耳。

translations.literal: Salt that is clean, unadulterated, and full in weight exists only at the few places where superiors come to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: Clean, unadulterated, full-weight salt is found only where senior officials personally supervise.

sentences.zh: 又常白鹽一千五百引，用船五十艘，每歲以四月起運，官鹽二萬引，用船五十艘，每歲以七月起運，而運司所遣之人，擅作威福，南抵臨清，北自通州，所至以索截河道，舟楫往來，無不被擾。

translations.literal: Moreover, 1,500 yin of changbai salt use fifty ships, transported each year starting in the fourth month; 20,000 yin of official salt use fifty ships, transported each year starting in the seventh month; yet persons dispatched by the transport commission abuse their power, from Linqing in the south to Tongzhou in the north, everywhere blocking waterways to extort; vessels coming and going were all harassed.
translations.idiomatic: Changbai salt of 1,500 yin uses fifty ships yearly from the fourth month; official salt of 20,000 yin uses fifty ships from the seventh month; yet transport commission agents abuse their power from Linqing south to Tongzhou north, blocking waterways to extort every passing vessel.

sentences.zh: 名為和顧，實乃強奪。

translations.literal: Called 'contracted hire,' in fact it was forcible seizure.
translations.idiomatic: Called contracted hire, it was in fact forcible seizure.

sentences.zh: 一歲之中，千里之內，凡富商巨賈之載米粟者，達官貴人之載家室者，一概遮截，得重賄而放行，所拘留者，皆貧弱無力之人耳。

translations.literal: Within one year and a thousand li, all wealthy merchants carrying grain, and eminent officials carrying household goods, were intercepted wholesale; only after heavy bribes were they released; those detained were all poor and powerless people.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year and a thousand li, grain-laden merchants and officials moving household goods were stopped wholesale and released only after heavy bribes; those detained were the poor and powerless.

sentences.zh: 其舟小而不固，滲溺侵盜，弊病多端。

translations.literal: Their boats were small and not sturdy; seepage, soaking, and embezzlement produced many abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Their boats were small and flimsy; leakage and theft produced endless abuses.

sentences.zh: 既達京廒，又不得依時交收，淹延歲月，困守無聊，鬻妻子、質舟楫者，往往有之。

translations.literal: After reaching the capital granaries they still could not be received on time; months dragged on; those trapped in idle waiting often sold wives and children or pawned their boats.
translations.idiomatic: After reaching the capital granaries they could not be received on time; months dragged on; many sold wives and children or pawned their boats while waiting.

sentences.zh: 此客船所以狼顧不前，使京師百物湧貴者，實由於此。

translations.literal: This is why merchant vessels hesitate and do not advance, and why goods in the capital surge in price—it truly stems from this.
translations.idiomatic: This is why merchant shipping stalls and capital prices soar—it stems from this.

sentences.zh: 竊計官鹽二萬引，每引腳價中統鈔七貫，總為鈔三千錠，而十五局官典俸給，以一歲計之又五百七十六錠，其就支賃房之資，短腳之價，席草諸物，又在外焉。

translations.literal: It is calculated that 20,000 yin of official salt, at seven strings of Zhongtong notes porterage per yin, totals 3,000 ingots of notes; the salaries of bureau clerks at the fifteen bureaus add another 576 ingots per year; rent for quarters, short-distance porterage, matting, and other items are besides.
translations.idiomatic: Official salt of 20,000 yin at seven strings porterage per yin totals 3,000 ingots; salaries for fifteen bureaus add 576 ingots yearly; rent, short haulage, and matting are extra.

sentences.zh: 當時置局設官，但為民食貴鹽，殊不料官賣之弊，反不如商販之賤，豈忍徒費國家，而使百物貴也。

translations.literal: At the time bureaus and officials were established only because the people ate costly salt; they never expected that official sale's abuses would make salt costlier than merchant sale—how could one bear to waste state funds and make all goods dear?
translations.idiomatic: Bureaus were set up only because salt was costly for the people; they never imagined official sale would prove worse than merchants—why waste state funds and make everything dear?

sentences.zh: 宜從憲臺具呈中書省，議罷其鹽局，及來歲起運之時，出榜文播告鹽商，從便入京興販。

translations.literal: It is appropriate for the Censorate to memorialize the Secretariat, discuss abolishing the salt bureaus, and when transport resumes next year issue proclamations informing salt merchants they may enter the capital freely to trade.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate should memorialize the Secretariat to abolish the salt bureaus and, when transport resumes next year, announce that salt merchants may freely enter the capital to trade.

sentences.zh: 若常白鹽所用船五十艘，亦宜於江南造小料船處如數造之。

translations.literal: As for the fifty ships used for changbai salt, they too should be built in equal number where small craft are built in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: The fifty ships for changbai salt should be built in equal number where Jiangnan builds small craft.

sentences.zh: 既成之後，付運司顧人運載，庶舟楫通而商賈集，則京師百物賤，而鹽亦不貴矣。」

translations.literal: After they are completed, entrust the transport commission to hire men to carry cargo, so that boats may pass freely and merchants gather; then goods in the capital will be cheap and salt will not be costly either.'
translations.idiomatic: Once built, let the transport commission hire carriers so shipping flows and merchants gather; then capital goods will be cheap and salt will not be costly.'

sentences.zh: 御史臺以其言具呈中書，而河間運司所申，亦如前議。

translations.literal: The Censorate submitted their words fully to the Secretariat, and the Hejian Transport Commission's report was also as in the previous proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate relayed this to the Secretariat, and the Hejian Transport Commission reported likewise.

sentences.zh: 戶部言：「運司及大都路講究，即同監察御史所言，元設鹽局，合準革罷，聽從客旅興販。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue stated: 'The transport commission and Dadu Circuit, after investigation, agree with the supervising censor; the original salt bureaus should be approved for abolition, and traveling merchants permitted to trade.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue stated: 'After investigation the transport commission and Dadu Circuit agree with the censor: abolish the salt bureaus and allow traveling merchants to trade.

sentences.zh: 其常白鹽系內府必用之物，起運如故，宜從都省聞奏。」

translations.literal: Changbai salt is an item the inner palace must use; transport shall continue as before and should be reported through the metropolitan secretariat.'
translations.idiomatic: Changbai salt is required by the inner palace; transport shall continue as before and be reported through the metropolitan secretariat.'

sentences.zh: 二月初五日，中書省上奏，如戶部所擬行之。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the second month, the Secretariat memorialized and implemented it as the Ministry of Revenue proposed.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the second month the Secretariat memorialized and approved the Ministry of Revenue proposal.

sentences.zh: 河間之鹽：至正二年，河間運司申戶部云：「本司歲辦額余鹽共三十八萬引，計課鈔一百一十四萬錠，以供國用，不為不重。

translations.literal: Salt in Hejian: In the second year of Zhizheng, the Hejian Transport Commission reported to the Ministry of Revenue: 'This commission annually fulfills a quota of 380,000 yin of salt including surplus salt, totaling 1.14 million ingots of tax notes for state use—not a light burden.
translations.idiomatic: Salt in Hejian: In Zhizheng 2 the Hejian Transport Commission reported: 'We fulfill 380,000 yin yearly including surplus salt, totaling 1.14 million ingots in tax notes—a heavy burden on state finance.

sentences.zh: 近年以來，各處私鹽及犯界鹽販賣者眾，蓋因軍民官失於禁治，以致侵礙官課，鹽法澀滯，實由於此。

translations.literal: In recent years private salt and boundary-violating salt sales are numerous everywhere, fundamentally because military and civil officials have failed in prohibition, encroaching on official revenue and causing salt law to stagnate—this is the real cause.
translations.idiomatic: Private and boundary-violating salt sales have proliferated because officials failed to enforce prohibition, encroaching on official revenue and stalling the salt law.

sentences.zh: 乞轉呈都省，頒降詔旨，宣諭所司，欽依規辦。」

translations.literal: We beg that it be forwarded to the metropolitan secretariat, that an edict be promulgated, and responsible offices ordered to handle matters strictly according to regulations.'
translations.idiomatic: We ask that this be forwarded to the metropolitan secretariat for an edict ordering strict compliance.'

sentences.zh: 本部具呈中書省，遂於四月十七日上奏，降旨戒飭之。

translations.literal: This ministry submitted a full memorial to the Secretariat; on the seventeenth day of the fourth month they memorialized and issued an edict of admonition.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry memorialized the Secretariat; on the seventeenth day of the fourth month an admonitory edict was issued.

sentences.zh: 七月，又據河間運司申：「本司辦課，全藉郡縣行鹽地方買食官鹽。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, another report was received from the Hejian Transport Commission: 'This commission's tax fulfillment depends entirely on designated salt-consuming districts buying official salt.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the Hejian commission again reported: 'Our tax revenue depends entirely on salt-consuming districts buying official salt.

sentences.zh: 去歲河間等路旱蝗闕食，累蒙賑恤，民力未蘇，食鹽者少。

translations.literal: Last year Hejian and other circuits suffered drought, locusts, and food shortage, repeatedly receiving relief; the people's strength has not recovered and salt consumption is low.
translations.idiomatic: Last year Hejian and other circuits suffered drought, locusts, and famine despite relief; the populace has not recovered and salt consumption is low.

sentences.zh: 又因古北口等處，把隘官及軍人不為用心詰捕，大都路所屬有司，亦不奉公巡禁，致令諸人裝載疙疸鹽於街市賣之，或量以鬥，或盛以盤，明相饋送。

translations.literal: Moreover, because officials at Gubeikou and elsewhere failed to pursue smugglers diligently, and Dadu subordinate offices did not patrol faithfully, people loaded kediyan salt to sell in the streets, measuring by dou or serving on plates, openly exchanging gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Officials at Gubeikou and elsewhere failed to pursue smugglers, and Dadu subordinates failed to patrol, so people sold kediyan salt in the streets by the dou or on plates, openly trading it.

sentences.zh: 今紫荊關捕獲犯人張狡群等所載疙疸鹽，計一千六百餘斤。

translations.literal: Now at Zijing Pass the smuggler Zhang Jiaoqun and others were captured carrying more than 1,600 jin of kediyan salt.
translations.idiomatic: At Zijing Pass smugglers led by Zhang Jiaoqun were captured with more than 1,600 jin of kediyan salt.

sentences.zh: 自至元六年三月迄今犯者，將及百起。

translations.literal: From the third month of the sixth year of Zhiyuan until now offenders have approached a hundred cases.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhiyuan 6, third month, offenders have approached a hundred cases.

sentences.zh: 若不申聞，恐年終課不如數，虛負其咎。」

translations.literal: If we do not report, we fear the year's tax will fall short and we will bear empty blame.'
translations.idiomatic: If we do not report, we fear missing the annual quota and bearing unjust blame.'

sentences.zh: 本部具呈中書省，照會樞密院給降榜文禁治之。

translations.literal: This ministry submitted a memorial to the Secretariat and notified the Privy Council to issue prohibitory placards.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry memorialized the Secretariat and notified the Privy Council to issue prohibitory placards.

sentences.zh: 三年，又據河間運司申：「生財節用，固治國之常經；

translations.literal: In the third year, another report from the Hejian Transport Commission: 'Generating wealth and practicing economy are the constant principles of governing a state;
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the Hejian commission again reported: 'Generating wealth and practicing economy are constant principles of statecraft;

sentences.zh: 薄賦輕徭，實理民之大本。

translations.literal: light taxes and easy corvée are the great foundation of governing the people.
translations.idiomatic: light taxes and easy corvée are the great foundation of governing the people.

sentences.zh: 本司歲額鹽三十五萬引，近年又添余鹽三萬引，元簽竈戶五千七百七十四戶，除逃亡外，止存四千三百有一戶。

translations.literal: This commission's annual salt quota is 350,000 yin; in recent years another 30,000 yin of surplus salt was added; originally 5,774 saltern households were registered; apart from those who fled, only 4,301 remain.
translations.idiomatic: Our annual quota is 350,000 yin; recently 30,000 yin surplus was added; of 5,774 registered saltern households only 4,301 remain after flight.

sentences.zh: 每年額鹽，勒令見在疲乏之戶勉強包煎。

translations.literal: Each year the fixed quota salt is compelled from presently existing exhausted households to boil salt under contract.
translations.idiomatic: Each year exhausted remaining households are compelled to fulfill the fixed quota under contract.

sentences.zh: 今歲若依舊煎辦，人力不足。

translations.literal: If this year we boil according to the old practice, manpower is insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: This year the old quota cannot be boiled with available manpower.

sentences.zh: 又兼行鹽地方旱蝗相仍，百姓焉有買鹽之資。

translations.literal: Moreover, in salt-consuming districts drought and locusts have followed one another; how can the people have funds to buy salt?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover salt districts suffer repeated drought and locusts; the people lack funds to buy salt.

sentences.zh: 如蒙矜閔，自至正二年為始，權免余鹽三萬引，俟豐稔之歲，煎辦如舊。」

translations.literal: If the court shows compassion, from the second year of Zhizheng temporarily exempt the 30,000 yin of surplus salt; when harvest years return, boil as before.'
translations.idiomatic: If the court shows compassion, exempt the 30,000 yin surplus from Zhizheng 2 onward until harvest years return.'

sentences.zh: 本部以錢糧支用不敷，權擬住煎一萬引，具呈中書省。

translations.literal: This ministry, because money and grain expenditures were insufficient, provisionally proposed suspending boiling of 10,000 yin and submitted a memorial to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Because expenditures were insufficient, the ministry provisionally proposed suspending 10,000 yin and memorialized the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 正月二十八日上奏，如戶部所擬行之。

translations.literal: On the twenty-eighth day of the first month they memorialized and implemented it as the Ministry of Revenue proposed.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-eighth day of the first month the Secretariat approved the ministry proposal.

sentences.zh: 既而運司又言：「至元三十一年，本司辦鹽額二十五萬引，自後累增至三十有五萬。

translations.literal: Thereafter the transport commission again stated: 'In the thirty-first year of Zhiyuan this commission fulfilled 250,000 yin; thereafter it was repeatedly increased to 350,000.
translations.idiomatic: The transport commission then stated: 'In Zhiyuan 31 we fulfilled 250,000 yin; the quota was later raised to 350,000.

sentences.zh: 元統元年，又增余鹽三萬引，已經具呈。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuantong, another 30,000 yin of surplus salt was added; this was already memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuantong 1 another 30,000 yin surplus was added; this was already memorialized.

sentences.zh: 蒙都省奏準，住煎一萬引。

translations.literal: Approved by the metropolitan secretariat, boiling of 10,000 yin was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: The metropolitan secretariat approved suspending 10,000 yin.

sentences.zh: 外有二萬引，若依前勒令見戶包煎，實為難堪。

translations.literal: Apart from this, the remaining 20,000 yin, if compelled from present households as before, is truly unbearable.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining 20,000 yin, if compelled from present households as before, is truly unbearable.

sentences.zh: 如並將余鹽二萬引住煎，誠為便益。」

translations.literal: If surplus salt of 20,000 yin is also suspended from boiling, it would truly be beneficial.'
translations.idiomatic: Suspending the remaining 20,000 yin surplus would truly be beneficial.'

sentences.zh: 戶部又以所言具呈中書省，權擬余鹽二萬引住煎一年，至正四年煎辦如故。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue again submitted their words to the Secretariat and provisionally proposed suspending boiling of 20,000 yin surplus for one year, resuming in the fourth year of Zhizheng as before.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry again memorialized and provisionally suspended 20,000 yin surplus for one year, resuming in Zhizheng 4.

sentences.zh: 四月十二日上奏，如戶部所擬行之。

translations.literal: On the twelfth day of the fourth month they memorialized and implemented it as the Ministry of Revenue proposed.
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth day of the fourth month the Secretariat approved.

sentences.zh: 山東之鹽：元統二年，戶部呈：「據山東運司準濟南路牒，依副達魯花赤完者、同知阇裏帖木兒所言，比大都、河間運司，改設巡鹽官一十二員，專一巡禁本部。

translations.literal: Salt in Shandong: In the second year of Yuantong, the Ministry of Revenue submitted: 'According to the Shandong Transport Commission, following the memorial of Deputy Darughachi Wanzhe and Vice Commissioner Jarlig Temür of Jinan Circuit, compared with Dadu and Hejian transport commissions, establish twelve salt-patrol officials dedicated to patrolling and prohibiting within this commission.
translations.idiomatic: Salt in Shandong: In Yuantong 2 the ministry submitted: 'Per the Shandong Transport Commission, following Jinan officials Wanzhe and Jarlig Temür, compared with Dadu and Hejian, establish twelve dedicated salt-patrol officials.

sentences.zh: 詳山東運司，歲辦鈔七十五萬餘錠，行鹽之地，周圍三萬餘里，止是運判一員，豈能遍歷，恐私鹽來往，侵礙國課。

translations.literal: The Shandong Transport Commission annually fulfills more than 750,000 ingots; the salt-selling territory extends over 30,000 li; there is only one transport judge—how can he traverse it all? We fear private salt coming and going will encroach on state revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong fulfills over 750,000 ingots yearly across 30,000 li with only one transport judge—he cannot cover it all; private salt will encroach on revenue.

sentences.zh: 本司既與濟南路講究便益，宜準所言。」

translations.literal: This commission, having deliberated with Jinan Circuit for convenience, should approve what was stated.'
translations.idiomatic: Having deliberated with Jinan Circuit, the commission recommends approval.'

sentences.zh: 中書省令戶部復議之，本部言：「河間運司定設奏差一十二名，巡鹽官一十六名，山東運司設奏差二十四名，今既比例添設巡鹽官外，據元設奏差內減去一十二名。」

translations.literal: The Secretariat ordered the Ministry of Revenue to reconsider; this ministry stated: 'The Hejian Transport Commission has twelve memorial envoys and sixteen salt-patrol officials; the Shandong commission has twenty-four memorial envoys; now, besides adding patrol officials proportionally, reduce twelve from the original memorial envoys.'
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat ordered reconsideration; the ministry stated: 'Hejian has twelve envoys and sixteen patrol officers; Shandong has twenty-four envoys; add patrol officers proportionally but reduce twelve envoys.'

sentences.zh: 具呈中書省，如所擬行之。

translations.literal: Submitted to the Secretariat and implemented as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialized and approved.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，又據山東運司備臨朐、沂水等縣申：「本縣十山九水，居民稀少，元系食鹽地方，後因改為行鹽，民間遂食貴鹽，公私不便。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year, another report from the Shandong Transport Commission relayed petitions from Linqu, Yishui, and other counties: 'Our counties are nine-tenths mountain and one-tenth water; residents are few; originally salt-consuming districts; later changed to salt-selling districts; the people thus eat costly salt—public and private inconvenience.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, second month, Linqu, Yishui, and other counties petitioned: 'We are nine-tenths mountain; residents are few; formerly salt-consuming, later changed to salt-selling; the people eat costly salt to public and private inconvenience.

sentences.zh: 如蒙仍舊改為食鹽，令居民驗戶口多寡，以輸納課鈔，則官民俱便，抑且可革私鹽之弊。」

translations.literal: If permitted to revert to salt-consuming districts, assessing households by population to pay tax notes, then official and people would both benefit and private salt abuses could be reformed.'
translations.idiomatic: If reverted to salt-consuming districts with tax assessed by household, official and people would benefit and private salt abuses end.'

sentences.zh: 運司移文分司，並益都路及下滕、嶧等州，從長講究，互言食鹽為便。

translations.literal: The transport commission sent documents to branch offices, Yidu Circuit, and Xiazeng, Yi, and other prefectures; after joint deliberation all said salt-consuming was convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Branch offices and prefectures deliberated and agreed salt-consuming was convenient.

sentences.zh: 及準本司運使辛朝列牒云：「所據零鹽，擬依登、萊等處，銓註局官，給印置局，散賣於民，非惟大課無虧，官釋私鹽之憂，民免刑配之罪。」

translations.literal: Following the transport commissioner Xin Chaolie's document: 'For scattered salt areas, it is proposed like Deng and Lai to appoint bureau officials, issue seals, set up bureaus, and sell to the people—not only will major revenue not suffer, but the state will release worry over private salt and the people avoid penal servitude.'
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Xin proposed: 'For scattered salt areas, like Deng and Lai appoint bureau officials, issue seals, set up bureaus, and sell to the people—revenue will not suffer, the state avoids private-salt worry, and the people avoid penal servitude.'

sentences.zh: 戶部議：「山東運司所言，於滕、嶧等處增置十有一局，如登、萊三十五局之例，於錢谷官內通行銓註局官，散賣食鹽，官民俱便。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue deliberated: 'As the Shandong Transport Commission stated, add eleven bureaus in Teng, Yi, and elsewhere following the thirty-five bureaus of Deng and Lai; appoint bureau officials from revenue officers; sell consuming salt—convenient for official and people.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry deliberated: 'Add eleven bureaus in Teng, Yi, and elsewhere following Deng and Lai's thirty-five; appoint officials from revenue officers—convenient for all.

sentences.zh: 既經有司講究，宜從所議。」

translations.literal: Having been deliberated by responsible offices, it should follow the proposal.'
translations.idiomatic: Responsible offices have deliberated; follow the proposal.'

sentences.zh: 具呈中書省，如所擬行之。

translations.literal: Submitted to the Secretariat and implemented as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialized and approved.

sentences.zh: 至元二年，御史臺據山東肅政廉訪司申：「準濟南路備章丘縣申『見奉山東運司為本司額辦鹽課二十八萬引，除客商承辦之外，見存十三萬引，絕無買者，將及年終，歲課不能如數。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiyuan, the Censorate, following the Shandong Surveillance Commission's report: 'Following Jinan Circuit's relay of Zhangqiu County's petition: "This commission fulfills 280,000 yin annually; apart from merchant contracts, 130,000 yin remain with no buyers; year-end revenue cannot meet quota.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 2 the Censorate relayed Zhangqiu County: 'The commission fulfills 280,000 yin yearly; 130,000 yin remain unsold and year-end revenue falls short.

sentences.zh: 所據新城、章丘、長山、鄒平、濟南俱近鹽場，與大、小清河相接，客旅興販，宜依商河、滕、嶧等處，改為食鹽，權派八千引，責付本處有司自備席索腳力，赴已擬固堤等場，於元統三年依例支出，均散於民』等事，竊照山東運司，初無上司明文，輒擅散民食鹽，追納課鈔，使民不得安業。

translations.literal: Xincheng, Zhangqiu, Changshan, Zouping, and Jinan are all near salterns and connect to the Great and Small Qing Rivers; traveling merchants trade; like Shanghe, Teng, and Yi they should become salt-consuming districts; temporarily assign 8,000 yin; charge local offices to provide matting and porterage; disburse from Gudi and other fields in Yuantong 3 as prescribed and distribute to the people"—yet the Shandong Transport Commission, without superior authorization, arbitrarily distributed consuming salt to the people, pursued tax notes, and prevented the people from settling in their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Xincheng, Zhangqiu, Changshan, Zouping, and Jinan were all near salterns and connected to the Great and Small Qing Rivers, with traveling merchants trading there; like Shanghe, Teng, and Yi, they should become salt-consuming districts, temporarily assigned 8,000 yin, with local offices providing matting and porterage and distributing salt from Gudi and other fields in Yuantong 3. Yet the Shandong Transport Commission, without superior authorization, arbitrarily distributed consuming salt to the people, pursued tax notes, and kept the people from settling in their work.

sentences.zh: 今於至元元年正月、二月，兩次奉到中書戶部符文，行鹽食鹽地分已有定例，毋得樁配於民。

translations.literal: Now in the first and second months of the first year of Zhiyuan, documents from the Secretariat Ministry of Revenue were received twice: districts for selling and consuming salt already have fixed rules; the people must not be compulsorily assigned.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 1 the Secretariat twice ordered fixed rules for salt districts and forbade compulsory assignment.

sentences.zh: 本司不遵省部所行，寢匿符文，依前差人馳驛，督責州縣，臨逼百姓，追征食鹽課鈔，不無擾害。

translations.literal: This commission did not obey the provincial and ministry orders, concealed the documents, and as before dispatched men by post to compel prefectures and counties to press the people for consuming-salt tax notes—unquestionably harmful.
translations.idiomatic: The commission disobeyed, concealed the documents, and pressed counties to collect consuming-salt taxes by post—clearly harmful.

sentences.zh: 據本司恣意行事，玩法擾民，理應取問，緣系辦課之時，宜從憲臺區處。

translations.literal: According to this commission's arbitrary conduct, defying law and harming the people, they should be interrogated; but because it is tax-fulfillment season, the Censorate should handle it.
translations.idiomatic: They should be interrogated for defying law and harming the people, but during tax season the Censorate should handle it.

sentences.zh: 又據監察御史所呈，亦為茲事。

translations.literal: Supervising censors also memorialized on this matter.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising censors also memorialized on this matter.

sentences.zh: 若便行取問，即系辦課時月，具呈中書省區處。」

translations.literal: If interrogation proceeds immediately, it is tax season; submit to the Secretariat for disposition.'
translations.idiomatic: Immediate interrogation falls in tax season; submit to the Secretariat.'

sentences.zh: 戶部議呈：「行鹽食鹽已有定所，宜從改正。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue deliberated and submitted: 'Districts for selling and consuming salt already have fixed places; they should be corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry submitted: 'Salt districts have fixed places; correct them.

sentences.zh: 若準御史臺所呈，取問運司，卻緣鹽法例應從長規畫，似難別議。」

translations.literal: If we follow the Censorate and interrogate the transport commission, yet salt law should be planned comprehensively—it is hard to decide separately.'
translations.idiomatic: Interrogating the commission is hard to separate from comprehensive salt-law planning.'

sentences.zh: 中書省如所擬行之。

translations.literal: The Secretariat implemented as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat approved.

sentences.zh: 陜西之鹽：至元二年九月，御史臺準陜西行臺咨備監察御史帖木兒不花建言：「近蒙委巡歷奉元東道，至元元年各州縣戶口額辦鹽課，其陜西運司官不思轉運之方，每年豫期差人，分道賫引，遍散州縣，甫及旬月，杖限追鈔，不問民之無有。

translations.literal: Salt in Shaanxi: In the ninth month of the second year of Zhiyuan, the Censorate approved the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat's consultation relaying supervising censor Temür Buhua's proposal: 'Recently commissioned to tour Fengyuan East Circuit; in the first year of Zhiyuan each prefecture and county fulfilled salt tax by household quota; Shaanxi salt officials gave no thought to transport methods; each year they prematurely dispatch men by route to distribute warrants throughout prefectures and counties; within barely ten days they beat deadlines to pursue notes without regard to whether the people have means.
translations.idiomatic: Salt in Shaanxi: In the ninth month of Zhiyuan 2 censor Temür Buhua proposed: 'Shaanxi salt officials distribute warrants to every prefecture and pursue payment within ten days regardless of means.

sentences.zh: 竊照諸處運司之例，皆運官召商發賣，惟陜西等處鹽司，近年散於民戶。

translations.literal: Considering precedents of transport commissions everywhere, all have transport officials summon merchants to sell; only Shaanxi and other places in recent years distribute to civilian households.
translations.idiomatic: Elsewhere transport officials summon merchants; only Shaanxi recently distributes to households.

sentences.zh: 且如陜西行省食鹽之戶，該辦課二十萬三千一百六十四錠有餘。

translations.literal: For example, salt-consuming households of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat should fulfill more than 203,164 ingots.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi salt-consuming households owe more than 203,164 ingots.

sentences.zh: 於內鞏昌、延安等處認定課鈔一萬六千二百七十一錠，慶陽、環州、鳳翔、興元等處歲辦課一萬七千九百八十五錠，其餘課鈔，先因關陜旱饑，民多流亡，準中書省咨，至順三年鹽課，十分為率，減免四分，於今三載，尚有虧負。

translations.literal: Within this, Gongchang and Yan'an are assessed 16,271 ingots; Qingyang, Huanzhou, Fengxiang, and Xingyuan fulfill 17,985 ingots yearly; the remainder—because Guan-Shaan suffered drought and famine and people fled—received Secretariat approval in the third year of Zhishun to reduce salt tax by four-tenths; three years on, deficits remain.
translations.idiomatic: Part is fixed assessment; the rest was reduced four-tenths after famine in Zhishun 3; deficits remain after three years.

sentences.zh: 蓋因戶口雕殘，十亡八九，縱或有復業者，家產已空，爾來歲頗豐收，而物價甚賤，得鈔為艱。

translations.literal: Because households are decimated, eight or nine in ten are gone; even those returning have empty estates; harvests have lately been good yet prices are very low—obtaining notes is hard.
translations.idiomatic: Households are decimated; returnees are destitute; notes are hard to obtain despite good harvests.

sentences.zh: 本司官皆勒有司征辦，無分高下，一概給散，少者不下二三引，每一引收價三錠，富家無以應辦，貧下安能措畫？

translations.literal: Commission officials compel offices to collect without regard to wealth, distributing uniformly; the least is no less than two or three yin; each yin costs three ingots; wealthy families cannot comply, the poor cannot manage.
translations.idiomatic: Officials compel uniform distribution of at least two or three yin at three ingots each—unbearable for rich and poor alike.

sentences.zh: 糶終歲之糧，不酬一引之價，緩則輸息而借貸，急則典鬻妻子。

translations.literal: Selling a year's grain cannot pay one yin's price; when slow they borrow at interest; when urgent they pawn wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: A year's grain cannot pay one yin; they borrow or pawn families.

sentences.zh: 縱引目到手，力窘不能裝運，止從各處鹽商，勒價收買。

translations.literal: Even when warrants arrive, they lack strength to transport and can only sell at coerced prices to local salt merchants.
translations.idiomatic: They cannot transport and sell cheaply to local merchants.

sentences.zh: 舊債未償，新引又至，民力有限，官賦無窮。

translations.literal: Old debts unpaid, new warrants arrive—the people's strength is limited, official levies endless.
translations.idiomatic: Old debts unpaid, new warrants arrive—endless levies.

sentences.zh: 又寧夏所產韋紅鹽池，不辦課程，除鞏昌等處循例認納乾課，從便食用外，其池鄰接陜西環州百餘里，紅鹽味甘而價賤，解鹽味苦而價貴，百姓私相販易，不可禁約。

translations.literal: Moreover Ningxia produces weihong salt ponds not subject to tax; apart from Gongchang paying dry tax and consuming freely, the ponds border Shaanxi Huanzhou for a hundred li; weihong salt is sweet and cheap, jie salt bitter and dear—people trade privately beyond prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: Ningxia weihong salt is sweet and cheap beside bitter dear jie salt—private trade is unstoppable.

sentences.zh: 以此參詳，河東鹽池，除撈鹽戶口食鹽外，辦課引數，今後宜從運官設法，募商興販。

translations.literal: On examination, for Hedong salt ponds apart from saltern households' consuming salt, quota yin hereafter should have transport officials devise methods and recruit merchants.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong ponds should sell quota yin through merchants recruited by transport officials.

sentences.zh: 但遇行鹽之處，諸人毋得侵擾韋紅鹽法。

translations.literal: In salt-selling districts people must not encroach on weihong salt law.
translations.idiomatic: Salt-selling districts must not encroach on weihong salt rules.

sentences.zh: 運司每歲分輪官吏監視，聽民采取，立法抽分，依例發賣，每引收價鈔三錠。

translations.literal: Each year the transport commission rotates officials to supervise, allowing people to gather, taxing by statute, selling at three ingots per yin.
translations.idiomatic: Rotate officials yearly to supervise gathering, tax by statute, sell at three ingots per yin.

sentences.zh: 自黃河以西，從民食用，通辦運司元額課鈔。

translations.literal: West of the Yellow River let people consume freely while fulfilling the commission's original quota.
translations.idiomatic: West of the Yellow River let people consume freely while fulfilling the original quota.

sentences.zh: 因時夾帶至黃河東南者，同私鹽法罪之，陜西興販解鹽者不禁。

translations.literal: Smuggling east of the Yellow River is punished like private salt; Shaanxi merchants selling jie salt are not forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Smuggling to the southeast of the Yellow River is punished as private salt; Shaanxi jie-salt merchants are not forbidden.

sentences.zh: 如此庶望官民兩便，而課亦無虧矣。」

translations.literal: Thus official and people may both benefit and revenue not suffer loss.'
translations.idiomatic: Thus official and people benefit and revenue is preserved.'

sentences.zh: 又據陜西漢中道肅政廉訪使胡通奉所陳云：「陜西百姓，許食解鹽，近脫荒儉，流移漸復，正宜安輯，而鹽吏不察民瘼，止以恢辦為名，不論貧富，散引收課，或納錢入官，動經歲月，猶未得鹽。

translations.literal: Also following Shaanxi Hanzhong Surveillance Commissioner Hu Tongfeng's memorial: 'Shaanxi people are permitted jie salt; after famine people gradually return and should be settled, yet salt clerks, caring nothing for people's suffering, pursue fulfillment only, distribute warrants regardless of rich or poor, or collect money to the government—often months pass without receiving salt.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Tongfeng memorialized: 'Salt clerks ignore people's suffering, collect money, and delay delivery for months.

sentences.zh: 蓋因地遠，腳力艱澀。

translations.literal: This is because the distance makes porterage difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Distance makes porterage difficult.

sentences.zh: 今後若令大河以東之民，分定課程，買食解鹽，其以西之民，計口攤課，任食韋紅之鹽，則官不被擾，民無蕩產之禍矣。

translations.literal: Hereafter if people east of the Great River pay fixed quota for jie salt and people west pay per mouth for weihong salt, officials are not harassed and people avoid ruin.
translations.idiomatic: East of the river buy jie salt by quota; west pay per mouth for weihong salt—officials unharassed, people unruined.

sentences.zh: 且解鹽結之於風，韋紅之鹽產之於地，東鹽味苦，西鹽味甘，又豈肯舍其美而就其惡乎？

translations.literal: Jie salt forms in wind; weihong salt comes from earth; eastern salt is bitter, western sweet—who would abandon the good for the bad?
translations.idiomatic: Jie salt forms in wind, weihong from earth—who chooses bitter over sweet?

sentences.zh: 使陜西百姓，一概均攤解鹽之課，令食韋紅之鹽，則鹽吏免巡禁之勞，而民亦受惠矣。」

translations.literal: If Shaanxi people uniformly share jie salt tax yet eat weihong salt, salt clerks avoid patrol labor and the people receive benefit.
translations.idiomatic: If Shaanxi pays jie tax uniformly but eats weihong salt, clerks avoid patrol toil and people benefit."

sentences.zh: 本臺詳所言鹽法，宜從省部定擬，具呈中書省，送戶部議之。

translations.literal: This commission's detailed statement on the salt law stated should follow the provincial ministries in fixing a draft, prepare a full submission to the Central Secretariat, and send it to the Ministry of Revenue for deliberation.
