translations.idiomatic: The vouchers were too few and lightly taxed—convenient for ordinary users but inadequate. Certificates carried a heavier levy and served mainly merchants, yet many remained unsold at year's end.

sentences.zh: 每歲合印茶由，以十分為率，量添二分，計二百六十一萬七千五十八斤。

translations.literal: Each year the total printed tea vouchers, taking ten parts as the rate, add two parts in measured amount—totaling two million six hundred seventeen thousand fifty-eight jin.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was to increase annual voucher production by two-tenths, adding two million six hundred seventeen thousand fifty-eight jin.

sentences.zh: 算依引目內官茶，每斤收鈔一錢三分八厘八毫八絲，計增鈔七千二百六十九錠七兩，比驗減去引目二萬九千七十六張，庶幾引不停閑，茶無私積。

translations.literal: Calculated following the certificate category's official tea, each jin collects one qian three fen eight li eight hao eight si of paper money—total increase seven thousand two hundred sixty-nine ingots seven liang; compared and verified, reduce certificates by twenty-nine thousand seventy-six—then certificates would not be idle and tea would have no private hoarding.
translations.idiomatic: Charging one qian three fen eight li eight hao eight si per jin on the added volume would yield seven thousand two hundred sixty-nine ingots seven liang, offset by cutting twenty-nine thousand seventy-six certificates—keeping certificates from sitting idle and curbing hoarding.

sentences.zh: 中書戶部定擬，江西茶運司歲辦公據十萬道，引一百萬，計鈔二十八萬九千二百餘錠。

translations.literal: The Central Secretariat and Ministry of Revenue fixed and drafted: the Jiangxi Tea Transport Commission each year provides one hundred thousand public documents and one million certificates, totaling two hundred eighty-nine thousand two hundred-odd ingots of paper money.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Secretariat and Ministry of Revenue approved: the Jiangxi tea transport commission would issue one hundred thousand documents and one million certificates annually, worth two hundred eighty-nine thousand two hundred ingots.

sentences.zh: 茶引便於商販，而山場小民全憑茶由為照，歲辦茶由一千三百八萬五千二百八十九斤，每斤一錢一分一厘一毫二絲，計鈔五千八百一十六錠七兩四錢一分，減引二萬三千二百六十四張。

translations.literal: Tea certificates are convenient for merchants' trade, while mountain-field common people entirely rely on tea vouchers as proof; yearly vouchers of thirteen million eight hundred five thousand two hundred eighty-nine jin, each jin one qian one fen one li one hao two si, totaling five thousand eight hundred sixteen ingots seven liang four qian one fen—reducing certificates by twenty-three thousand two hundred sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Certificates suited merchants, but hill farmers depended entirely on vouchers. Annual vouchers of thirteen million eight hundred five thousand two hundred eighty-nine jin at one qian one fen one li one hao two si per jin would yield five thousand eight hundred sixteen ingots seven liang four qian one fen, with twenty-three thousand two hundred sixty-four fewer certificates.

sentences.zh: 茶引一張，造茶九十斤，納官課十二兩五錢。

translations.literal: One tea certificate produces ninety jin of tea and pays official revenue of twelve taels five qian.
translations.idiomatic: Each certificate authorized ninety jin of tea and a levy of twelve taels five qian.

sentences.zh: 如於茶由量添二分，計二百六十一萬七千五十八斤，每斤添收鈔一錢三分八厘八毫八絲，計鈔七千二百六十九錠七兩，積出余零鈔數，官課無虧，而便於民用。」

translations.literal: If on tea vouchers the measured addition of two parts—totaling two million six hundred seventeen thousand fifty-eight jin—each jin additionally collects one qian three fen eight li eight hao eight si of paper money, totaling seven thousand two hundred sixty-nine ingots seven liang; accumulated surplus fractional paper money—official revenue would not be deficient, and it would be convenient for the people's use."
translations.idiomatic: Adding two-tenths to the vouchers—two million six hundred seventeen thousand fifty-eight jin at one qian three fen eight li eight hao eight si per jin—would bring seven thousand two hundred sixty-nine ingots seven liang without reducing official revenue, while easing life for ordinary users."

sentences.zh: 合準本省所擬，具呈中書省，移咨行省，如所擬行之。

translations.literal: Combined approval followed this province's proposal; fully presented to the Central Secretariat, forwarded by memorial to the branch secretariat—implement as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was approved as the province proposed, sent to the Central Secretariat, and relayed to the branch secretariat for implementation.

sentences.zh: 至正二年，李宏陳言內一節，言江州茶司據引不便事云：「榷茶之制，古所未有，自唐以來，其法始備。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhizheng, Li Hong's memorial included one section on the Jiangzhou Tea Bureau's inconvenience with certificates, stating: "The monopoly-tea system was never in antiquity; from the Tang onward its methods became complete.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhizheng Li Hong's memorial included a section on problems with tea certificates at the Jiangzhou bureau: "State monopolization of tea did not exist in antiquity; the Tang dynasty first established a full regulatory system.

sentences.zh: 國朝既於江州設立榷茶都轉運司，仍於各路出茶之地設立提舉司七處，專任散據賣引，規辦國課，莫敢誰何。

translations.literal: Our dynasty, having established the Monopoly Tea Chief Transport Directorate at Jiangzhou, still established seven supervisory directorates at each route where tea is produced, solely responsible for distributing and selling certificates and planning national revenue—none dared object.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty founded the Jiangzhou tea transport directorate and seven regional supervisory offices at tea-producing circuits, each charged with selling certificates and meeting the national quota—none could resist them.

sentences.zh: 每至十二月初，差人勾集各處提舉司官吏，關領次年據引。

translations.literal: Every year by the twelfth month people are dispatched to summon the supervisory directorate officials of each place to receive the next year's certificates.
translations.idiomatic: Each December officials were sent to summon the supervisory commissioners and issue the next year's certificates.

sentences.zh: 及其到司，旬月之間，司官不能偕聚。

translations.literal: When they arrive at the directorate, within a month or so the directorate officials cannot all gather together.
translations.idiomatic: After they reached the directorate, a month might pass before all commissioners could assemble.

sentences.zh: 吏貼需求，各滿所欲，方能給付據引。

translations.literal: Clerks and runners make demands; each satisfies their desires before certificates can be delivered.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks and runners extorted bribes until every demand was met before certificates were handed over.

sentences.zh: 此時春月已過。

translations.literal: By then the spring month has already passed.
translations.idiomatic: By then spring was already gone.

sentences.zh: 及還本司，方欲點對給散，又有分司官吏，到各處驗戶散據賣引。

translations.literal: Upon returning to the directorate they just wish to check and distribute; again branch-commission officials go to each place to verify households and distribute and sell certificates.
translations.idiomatic: Back at the directorate they would begin distribution—while branch officials toured the circuits to verify households and sell certificates on site.

sentences.zh: 每引十張，除正納官課一百二十五兩外，又取要中統鈔二十五兩，名為搭頭事例錢，以為分司官吏饋𩟝之資。

translations.literal: For every ten certificates, besides the official levy of one hundred twenty-five taels, they again take twenty-five liang of Zhongtong paper money, called "attached-head precedent money," as funds for branch-commission officials' provisions and entertainment.
translations.idiomatic: For every ten certificates, beyond the official levy of one hundred twenty-five taels, clerks extracted twenty-five liang of Zhongtong notes as "surcharge precedent fees" to fund branch officials' entertainment.

sentences.zh: 提舉司雖以榷茶為名，其實不能專散據賣引之任，不過為運司官吏營辦資財而已。

translations.literal: Although the supervisory directorate is named for monopoly tea, in truth it cannot solely bear the duty of distributing and selling certificates—it is merely raising assets for transport-commission officials.
translations.idiomatic: Though called tea monopolies, the supervisory offices could not actually control certificate sales—they merely raised revenue for transport commissioners.

sentences.zh: 上行下效，勢所必然。

translations.literal: The upper sets the example and the lower follows—the tendency is necessarily so.
translations.idiomatic: What superiors do, subordinates imitate—inevitably so.

sentences.zh: 提舉司既見分司官吏所為若是，亦復仿效遷延。

translations.literal: The supervisory directorate, seeing branch-commission officials act thus, also imitated and delayed.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing branch officials behave this way, the supervisory offices copied their delays.

sentences.zh: 及茶戶得據還家，已及五六月矣。

translations.literal: When tea households obtain certificates and return home, it is already the fifth or sixth month.
translations.idiomatic: Tea growers did not get their certificates home until the fifth or sixth month.

sentences.zh: 中間又存留茶引二三千本，以茶戶消乏為名，轉賣與新興之戶。

translations.literal: Meanwhile they again retain two or three thousand certificates, citing tea households' exhaustion as the reason, and resell them to newly rising households.
translations.idiomatic: Officials also hoarded two or three thousand certificates, claiming growers were exhausted, and resold them to newcomers.

sentences.zh: 每據又多取中統鈔二十五兩，上下分派，各為己私。

translations.literal: For each certificate they again take twenty-five liang of Zhongtong paper money; upper and lower divide it, each for private gain.
translations.idiomatic: Each certificate brought another twenty-five liang in Zhongtong notes, split between superiors and subordinates for private profit.

sentences.zh: 不知此等之錢，自何而出，其為茶戶之苦，有不可言。

translations.literal: One does not know whence such money comes; the suffering of tea households is unspeakable.
translations.idiomatic: No one could say where this money came from; the growers' suffering defied description.

sentences.zh: 至如得據在手，碾磨方興，吏卒踵門，催並初限。

translations.literal: As for obtaining certificates in hand, grinding just rising—clerks and runners follow at the door pressing the first deadline.
translations.idiomatic: Once certificates were in hand and grinding had barely begun, clerks and runners appeared at the door demanding the first installment.

sentences.zh: 不知茶未發賣，何從得錢？

translations.literal: One does not know—the tea has not yet been sold; whence get money?
translations.idiomatic: The tea had not been sold—where was the money to come from?

sentences.zh: 間有充裕之家，必須別行措辦。

translations.literal: Occasionally among ample households they must separately arrange funds.
translations.idiomatic: Only well-off households could raise the cash elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 其力薄者，例被拘監，無非典鬻家私，以應官限。

translations.literal: Those of slight strength are routinely detained; it is not without improper selling of private property to meet the official deadline.
translations.idiomatic: The poor were routinely imprisoned and often forced to sell family property illegally to meet official deadlines.

sentences.zh: 及終限不能足備，上司緊並，重復勾追，非法苦楚。

translations.literal: When the final deadline cannot be fully provided, superiors press tightly, repeatedly summoning and pursuing—unlawful bitter suffering.
translations.idiomatic: Those who missed the final deadline faced relentless pressure, repeated summons, and unlawful torment.

sentences.zh: 此皆由運司給引之遲，分司苛取之過。

translations.literal: All this is because the transport commission delays giving certificates and the branch commission harshly extracts in excess.
translations.idiomatic: The root cause was late issuance by the transport commission and excessive levies by the branch offices.

sentences.zh: 茶戶本圖求利，反受其害，日見消乏逃亡，情實堪憫。

translations.literal: Tea households originally sought profit yet instead receive harm; daily they grow exhausted, flee, and disappear—the situation is truly pitiable.
translations.idiomatic: Growers who sought profit found only injury; exhaustion and flight grew daily—a plight that merited compassion.

sentences.zh: 今若申明舊制，每歲正月，須要運司盡將據引給付提舉司，隨時派散，無得停留在庫，多收分例，妨誤造茶時月；

translations.literal: Now if the old system is clarified—each year in the first month the transport commission must completely give all certificates to the supervisory directorate, distribute promptly with none retained in the warehouse, no excess collection of portions, and no obstructing the months of tea production;
translations.idiomatic: Li Hong proposed restoring the old rule: every first month the transport commission must deliver all certificates to the supervisory offices for immediate distribution, with none held in storehouses, no surcharges, and no delay into the tea-making season;

sentences.zh: 如有過期，別行定罪。

translations.literal: if overdue, separately impose punishment by law.
translations.idiomatic: late delivery would be separately punishable by law.

sentences.zh: 仍不許運司似前分司自行散賣據引，違者從肅政廉訪司依例糾治。

translations.literal: Still do not permit the transport commission, as before the branch commission, to sell and distribute certificates on its own; violators shall be investigated and punished by the Surveillance Commission according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The transport commission must not, like the branch offices before, sell certificates on its own; violators would be prosecuted by the surveillance commission.

sentences.zh: 如此，庶茶司少革貪黷之風，茶戶免損乏之害。」

translations.literal: Thus perhaps the tea bureau would somewhat reform its greedy and corrupt ways, and tea households would avoid depletion and harm."
translations.idiomatic: That way the tea bureau might curb its corruption and growers would escape ruin."

sentences.zh: 中書省以其言送戶部定擬，復移咨江西行省，委官與茶運司講究，如果便益，如所言行之。

translations.literal: The Central Secretariat took his words and sent them to the Ministry of Revenue for fixing and drafting, again forwarded by memorial to the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat, commissioning officials together with the tea transport commission to investigate; if truly convenient, implement as proposed."
translations.idiomatic: The Central Secretariat referred the memorial to the Ministry of Revenue and notified the Jiangxi branch secretariat to work with the tea transport commission. If the reforms proved beneficial, they were to be enacted as proposed.
